analysis.title: Interest Rates Weekly: The great reset
key_insights: Hopes that the US midterms will bring the war in Iran to an end triggered a sharp fall in oil and gas futures, which pushed global front-end rates lower. The size of the move across countries did not track energy trade balances.
UK and Canada front ends outperformed because markets removed the premium for their central banks having to catch up after a delayed start to tightening.
Nine months of elevated energy prices keep the hawkish bias intact for front-end meetings. One hike over the coming quarter remains the base case for G4 jurisdictions.

Correlation of STIR pricing to energy prices should concentrate in the very front end. Implied hikes beyond the next live meeting are seen as inertia, and the medium-term inflation and growth balance takes over after a couple of quarters.

A durable Iran resolution with a lower floor for energy prices and tighter financial conditions would increase policy divergence. Energy importers would focus on second-round effects and activity data, and current EZ GDP growth and core inflation expectations do not support embedding cuts.
The key US question is whether the expansion continues with a lower fiscal impulse and whether other sectors can pick up if AI capex slows.

Long-term real yields in G4 have room to rally further as risky asset and bond correlation falls. Caveats for USD rates are the debt ceiling and budget, and the effect of Kevin Warsh's taskforces on Fed policy.
The bank favours steeper 5-30Y and 10-30Y IRS curves, driven by lower terminal rates and subsiding volatility.

JGB and Bund swap spreads should tighten on collateral excess, lower volatility and safe-haven demand. UST swap spreads are seen as a widener, driven by rates direction, bank balance sheet space and Treasury debt management, since a divided government makes large debt-funded fiscal packages harder and a frugal budget is very unlikely.

EUR rates: the team leans cautiously long duration, especially in the belly. Core inflation next year is expected to keep the ECB from supporting growth, so easing is hard to embed, while front-end repricing lower is limited. Wages data is a potential catalyst.

The bank sees room for the belly to outperform, a steeper 5-30Y IRS curve and a lower belly in the 2-5-10Y fly. OATs could tighten further if Iran resolution hopes materialise, but the budget process and limited front-end downside cap the move.

EGB spreads should tighten slightly. Budget disputes in Belgium and France and Spanish elections limit the benefit from lower implied volatility, but front-end spreads should gain from Schatz asset swap spread normalisation.

France: the National Assembly rejected the revenue part of the finance law this week, so the government's original text goes to the Senate. The government can then use Article 49.3, which risks a no-confidence motion, or wait for the 70-day deadline on 17 December and adopt the budget by ordinance, which has never been done under the Fifth Republic.

Belgium: Prime Minister Bart De Wever tendered his resignation after budget talks failed. The King's decision is due 6 November, and a deadlock could lead to provisional twelfths, which delay fiscal reforms and carry a cost.

Italy: ECOFIN rules on 9 November on the EUR29bn escape clause deviation request. Spain: general election on 29 November, so no 2027 budget is possible this legislature. Germany: budget committee 12 November, plenary 24-27 November. Netherlands: lower house votes 12 November on the tax plan of the minority cabinet.

Eurozone October flash headline inflation was 4.0% YoY, an upside surprise driven by gas and electricity. Core was 2.54% against 2.5% consensus, with the bank expecting core of about 2.9-3.0% on average next year versus 2.6% in the ECB's September forecasts.

Since 30 September, the first Brent future fell USD15/bl excluding the roll, European gas fell EUR15/MWh and German Q1-27 power fell EUR27/MWh. By the bank's sensitivities this implies about 60bp off mid-2027 headline inflation, against a 50bp fall in the mid-2027 EUR inflation swap, which the bank calls a logical reaction.

Eurozone 1YF1Y inflation forward fell 10bp on the week to 2.1% and 5YF5Y moved 3bp to 2.1%, so market-based expectations are not de-anchoring. French inflation forwards rose, which the bank attributes to a higher Livret A ceiling announced by PM Lecornu and likely extra demand for inflation hedges from French banks.
The bank closed its sell 3YF2Y FRCPIx vs HICPx trade on 3 November.
US headline CPI is now expected to peak no higher than 3.7% YoY in coming months, versus a prior expectation of about 3.9% in November. An updated US CPI path comes with the October CPI preview.

tension_points.bull_case: Lower energy prices allow some front-end repricing lower, supporting a cautious long EUR duration stance and an OAT tightening if Iran resolution hopes materialise.
tension_points.bear_case: Nine months of elevated energy prices keep the hawkish bias intact, with one G4 hike still the base case, which limits any front-end rally.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Re-escalation of the war in Iran.

tension_points.theme: US expansion after fiscal and AI capex
tension_points.bull_case: Long-term real yields can rally further as bond and risky asset correlation falls and policy becomes more readable.
tension_points.bear_case: The expansion may not hold with a lower fiscal impulse and an AI capex slowdown, and the debt ceiling and Warsh taskforces add policy uncertainty.
